47	## Abstract
48	
49	Extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EMC) is defined in the large majority of cases by an in-frame fusion
50	of *EWSR1* (less often *TAF15*) to the orphan nuclear receptor *NR4A3*, on an otherwise "quiet" genome
51	[Sjögren; Panagopoulos]. The companion NR4A3-degrader program in this repo recruits the **NR4A3
52	ligand-binding domain (LBD)** to an E3 ligase ([`nr4a3-degrader-paper.md`](./nr4a3-degrader-paper.md)).
53	That LBD sequence is **identical in the fusion and in wild-type NR4A3** — the fusion retains a near-intact
54	LBD — so the agent is NR4A3-selective (it can be tuned to spare the NR4A1/NR4A2 paralogues) but **not
55	fusion-selective**: it also removes tumour-suppressive wild-type NR4A3, whose loss is implicated in AML and
56	in HCC/breast/lymphoma [Mullican 2007; Safe & Karki 2021]. This manuscript designs the protein-level route
57	to the feature the LBD degrader structurally cannot reach: **true fusion-exclusivity.** We exploit
58	**coincidence detection (an "AND-gate")**. Arm 1 binds the shared NR4A3 LBD (the opened cryptic pocket of
59	the companion paper); arm 2 binds the EWSR1 low-complexity/transactivation
60	domain (LC/IDR) or its phase-separated micro-environment — a feature whose *fusion-specificity comes from its

62	Erratum). Each arm is chosen

67	illustrative arm affinities Kd1 = 10 µM (LBD), Kd2 = 100 µM (EWS-LC) and EM = 1 mM, the fusion is engaged
68	at an avidity Kd ≈ 1 µM and is bound 5.5× more than wild-type NR4A3 — a **binding** window tunable to

70	inputs are assumptions, not affinities; (ii) this is a *binding* window, not a *degradation* window

72	arm 2 — the EWS-LC domain is intrinsically disordered (mean pLDDT 38.8, 98.1% of residues < 50;
73	[`novel-modalities.md`](../modality-census/novel-modalities.md) §2) with no pocket, so arm 2 cannot be a classical pocket
74	ligand and must be an emerging condensate-partitioning / IDR-contacting moiety. We lay out the deferred
75	(GPU-requiring) in-silico program and the decisive experiment for others. The AND-gate logic generalises
76	to any fusion that joins a ligandable domain to an IDR — the FET-fusion sarcomas broadly.
77	
78	---
79	
80	## 1. Background and the fusion-selectivity gap
81	
82	EMC's defining lesion fuses the N-terminal low-complexity/transactivation domain of EWSR1 (a FET-family
83	prion-like IDR) to most of NR4A3, including a near-intact ligand-binding domain [Sjögren; Panagopoulos;
84	Boulay 2017 for the EWS prion-like domain's condensate/BAF-retargeting behaviour]. On a quiet genome the
85	chimera is, to a first approximation, the disease — an attractive single target.
86	
87	The repo's lead protein-level agent is a **degrader of the NR4A3 LBD**
88	([`nr4a3-degrader-paper.md`](./nr4a3-degrader-paper.md)): because the collapsed orphan-receptor pocket
89	precludes occupancy pharmacology, the apt modality is to recruit the ordered LBD to an E3 ligase and remove
90	the protein. That program shows the LBD's borderline static pocket (fpocket druggability 0.495, below the
91	calibrated drug-bound band 0.53–0.68) **breathes** under metadynamics into transiently druggable
92	conformations, and it maps NR4A3-vs-NR4A1/NR4A2 divergent residues as handles for **paralogue**
93	selectivity.
94	
95	**But paralogue selectivity is not fusion selectivity.** The LBD that the degrader's warhead engages is
96	the *same* domain — the same sequence, ~100% identity over the LBD — in the EMC fusion and in wild-type
97	NR4A3. A warhead that binds the fusion's LBD will, by construction, bind wild-type NR4A3's LBD equally
98	well. So the LBD degrader degrades *all* NR4A3 (and is rightly framed target-centrically, covering both
99	EMC and NR4A3-over-expression diseases such as acinic cell carcinoma). The residual liability is real:
100	wild-type NR4A3 is **tumour-suppressive** outside EMC — combined Nr4a1/Nr4a3 loss causes AML in mice
101	[Mullican 2007], and NR4A3 is tumour-suppressive in HCC/breast/lymphoma [Safe & Karki 2021]. An ideal EMC
102	agent would remove the fusion while leaving wild-type NR4A3 intact.
103	
104	No single shared epitope can deliver that, because the only fusion-unique *protein* feature is the
105	**juxtaposition** of the EWSR1 LC domain and the NR4A3 LBD on one chain — neither half is itself unique to
106	the fusion (wild-type EWSR1 has the LC domain; wild-type NR4A3 has the LBD). The design problem is
107	therefore not "find a fusion-only pocket" but "**detect the co-occurrence** of two non-unique features on
108	one molecule." That is exactly what a coincidence-detecting bivalent ligand does.
109	
110	---
111	
112	## 2. The AND-gate design
113	
114	The molecule is a single bivalent ligand with two binding arms joined by a linker, plus (in the degrader
115	version) an E3-recruiting element. Coincidence is enforced by avidity.
116	
117	- **Arm 1 — the shared LBD warhead.** This is the **opened-LBD cryptic-pocket warhead** of the companion
118	  degrader paper ([`nr4a3-degrader-paper.md`](./nr4a3-degrader-paper.md) §2.2–2.4). Cited at honest weight:
119	  that pocket's druggability rises under bias to a **biased-MD peak of 0.931** (maximum over 600 opened
120	  frames — an extreme-value statistic best read as a *fraction-of-frames-druggable distribution*, not a
121	  single number), via **basin-internal breathing** rather than a separate opened free-energy basin (F(Rg)
122	  is monotonic), at a low apparent cost (~0.76 kcal/mol to a druggable conformation, read off an
123	  incompletely-converged biased profile and therefore **provisional** pending the unbiased release run)
124	  [see [`nr4a3-degrader-paper-redteam.md`](./nr4a3-degrader-paper-redteam.md) F1–F5]. Arm 1 binds the LBD
125	  that the fusion and wild-type NR4A3 share. **Crucially, here we want this arm *weak*** — strong enough to
126	  contribute to avidity on the fusion, too weak to occupy wild-type NR4A3 on its own.
127	
128	- **Arm 2 — the fusion-restricted anchor.** Arm 2 binds the **EWSR1 low-complexity / transactivation
129	  domain** (residues 1–264 of the fusion's EWS portion) or, more realistically, the **condensate
130	  micro-environment** that this prion-like IDR nucleates [Boulay 2017]. This feature is present only in the
131	  fusion: wild-type NR4A3 has no EWS LC domain. Arm 2 is the harder arm (§4) precisely because the LC
132	  domain is disordered and pocket-less.
133	
134	- **The coincidence logic.** On the **fusion**, both features sit on one chain. Once either arm binds, the
135	  partner arm is held at a high local concentration — the **effective molarity (EM)** — so the second
136	  engagement is intramolecular and avidity-enhanced; the apparent bivalent dissociation constant follows
137	  the standard tethered-ligand relation **Kd_avidity ≈ Kd1·Kd2 / EM** (valid when EM ≫ Kd2). On
138	  **wild-type NR4A3**, there is no arm-2 partner, so only arm 1 can engage — **monovalently, at the weak
139	  Kd1**. Choosing both arms weak enough that neither meaningfully occupies its target alone means wild-type
140	  NR4A3 (arm 1 only) stays largely unbound, while the fusion (both arms, avidity) is engaged. The molecule
141	  thus computes a logical AND over "LBD present" and "EWS-LC present" — true only for the fusion.
142	
143	This is the only one of the three protein-level fusion-unique routes (the other two being a juxtaposition-
144	created composite surface, and a condensate-conditional degrader) that converts two *individually
145	non-selective* contacts into a *selective* one purely through geometry/avidity, without requiring a
146	genuinely fusion-unique pocket to exist.
147	
148	---
149	
150	## 3. Quantitative selectivity model (the new CPU result)
151	
152	The one new computation here is a pure-stdlib, CPU-only equilibrium avidity model
153	([`andgate_selectivity_model.py`](../../modalities/andgate_selectivity_model.py) →
154	[`fusion-andgate-selectivity-model.json`](../../modalities/fusion-andgate-selectivity-model.json)). It asks a
155	single quantitative question: *can two arms that are each individually too weak to matter become
156	fusion-selective by avidity?* The selectivity window is defined as (fraction of fusion bound) / (fraction
157	of wild-type NR4A3 bound) at a given free-ligand concentration; the fusion is modelled by Kd_avidity =
158	Kd1·Kd2/EM, wild-type by Kd1 alone.
159	
160	**The inputs are illustrative assumptions, not measured affinities** (the JSON carries
161	`_inputs_are_illustrative: true`). They are parameterised to plausible ranges from the bivalent/PROTAC/
162	avidity literature [Békés/Langley/Crews 2022] to test the *design principle*, and assert nothing about any
163	real compound.
164	
165	**Base case** (Kd1 = 10 µM on the LBD, Kd2 = 100 µM on EWS-LC, EM = 1 mM, free ligand 1 µM):
166	
167	| quantity | value |
168	|---|---|
169	| Kd_avidity (fusion) | ≈ 1 µM (= Kd1·Kd2/EM) |
170	| fusion fraction bound | 0.50 |
171	| wild-type NR4A3 fraction bound | 0.091 |
172	| **fusion-vs-wild-type window** | **5.5×** |
173	
174	So with each arm individually weak, wild-type NR4A3 — engaged only monovalently by arm 1 — stays ~9%
175	bound, while avidity pulls the fusion to ~50% bound: a **5.5× binding window** from arms that, alone, would
176	be dismissed as too weak to develop.
177	
178	**The window is tunable.** Sweeping the effective molarity (the key linker-geometry knob) at fixed arms:
179	
180	| EM (M) | Kd_avidity | fusion bound | WT bound | window |
181	|---|---|---|---|---|
182	| 1e-4 | 10 µM | 0.091 | 0.091 | 1.0× (no avidity — arms equal, no selectivity) |
183	| 3e-4 | 3.3 µM | 0.231 | 0.091 | 2.5× |
184	| **1e-3** | **1.0 µM** | **0.500** | **0.091** | **5.5× (base case)** |
185	| 3e-3 | 0.33 µM | 0.750 | 0.091 | 8.2× |
186	| 1e-2 | 0.10 µM | 0.909 | 0.091 | 10.0× |
187	| 3e-2 | 33 nM | 0.968 | 0.091 | 10.6× |
188	| 1e-1 | 10 nM | 0.990 | 0.091 | **10.9× (ceiling)** |
189	
190	The window rises from 1× (no avidity) to a ceiling of **~11×** as EM increases — i.e. a shorter, better
191	pre-organised linker that raises the second arm's local concentration widens fusion-selectivity, because
192	the wild-type baseline (arm-1-only, fixed at 0.091) does not move. Sweeping arm-1 strength tells the same
193	story from the other side: making arm 1 *weaker* (Kd1 100 µM) drops wild-type occupancy to ~1% and widens
194	the window to ~9×, while making arm 1 *strong* (Kd1 1 µM) lifts wild-type to 50% bound and collapses the
195	window to 1.8× — confirming the design rule.
196	
197	**EM is not a free parameter — it is set by the linker, and the physics is encouraging.** A second
198	CPU/stdlib model ([`andgate_linker_em.py`](../../modalities/andgate_linker_em.py) →
199	[`fusion-andgate-linker-em.json`](../../modalities/fusion-andgate-linker-em.json)) grounds EM in ideal-chain
200	polymer physics: for a flexible linker of contour length L\_c and Kuhn length ~0.5 nm, the coincident-site
201	effective molarity EM = (3/(2π·L\_c·b))^{3/2}·(1e24/N\_A). Over the synthesizable range this gives EM from
202	~1.5 M (1 nm, ~3 PEG units) down to ~9×10⁻³ M (30 nm, ~86 units) — and, fed back into the avidity model,
203	the fusion-vs-WT window stays **~10–11× across the entire range** (10.8× at 10 nm, 9.9× even at 30 nm).
204	The design reading: because even a long tether keeps EM well above the weak arm-2 Kd (100 µM), the window
205	is **robust to linker length** rather than fragile — the ceiling (~11×) is set by arm-1 strength, not the
206	linker, so widening it means *weakening arm 1*, not shortening the tether. Honest caveat: this EM is the
207	*coincident-site upper bound*; a mobile, disordered EWS-LC anchor will realise a lower EM, so these are
208	optimistic ceilings (the §4 mobility point).
209	
210	**Design rule (from the model):** *pick **both** arms individually too weak to occupy wild-type NR4A3 at
211	the dosed concentration, and rely on avidity (EM) to engage only the fusion, which uniquely presents both
212	features on one chain.* Larger EM (shorter/optimised linker) and weaker single arms widen the
213	fusion-vs-WT window — at the cost of needing a higher total dose to reach the avidity-bound fusion.
214	
215	**From a binding window to a degradation window (a third CPU model).** Because a degrader acts through a
216	ternary complex, we modelled whether the binding window survives into *degradation*
217	([`andgate_degradation_model.py`](../../modalities/andgate_degradation_model.py) →
218	[`fusion-andgate-degradation-model.json`](../../modalities/fusion-andgate-degradation-model.json)): a
219	cooperative 1:1:1 target–degrader–E3 equilibrium where the fusion is engaged at the avidity Kd and
220	wild-type NR4A3 at the weak monovalent Kd1, with the **E3 arm and cooperativity shared** (both present the
221	same LBD/E3 handle). The result is sobering and honest: the degradation window **does not inherit the full
222	binding window** — it peaks near it (~6.8×) only at **low, sub-saturating** degrader and **erodes toward
223	~1× at saturating dose** (the hook effect — ternary falling as the degrader separately saturates target and
224	E3 — hits *both* species), and it **shrinks with stronger positive cooperativity** (5.4× at α=1 → 1.7× at
225	α=30, because cooperativity proportionally rescues the weaker-binding wild-type). Design implications: run
226	the AND-gate at **sub-saturating dose** and avoid strong cooperativity; and since the shared E3 side cannot
227	add selectivity, **all** of it must come from the avidity arm. So degradation selectivity is *narrower and
228	more dose-fragile* than the binding window — a genuine caveat, not a footnote.
229	
230	**Two honest caveats, stated up front, not buried:**
231	1. **This is a binding window, not a degradation window.** Occupancy selectivity is necessary but not
232	   sufficient for *degradation* selectivity, which is additionally set by whether each species forms a
233	   productive ternary complex with the E3 ligase (a non-selective binder can degrade selectively, and vice
234	   versa). The 5.5–11× is fusion-vs-WT *occupancy*, the upstream filter — not a degradation margin.
235	2. **The numbers ride on assumed inputs.** They demonstrate the *principle scales as claimed*; they are not
236	   a prediction for any specific molecule. A modest window (single digits, low double digits) is the
237	   honest expectation for a real, manufacturable AND-gate — and is presented as such, not inflated.
238	
239	---
240	
241	## 4. The hard part (honest)
242	
243	The AND-gate's selectivity is only as good as its weakest assumption, which is **arm 2**.
244	
245	- **Arm 2 has no pocket to bind.** The EWSR1 LC/transactivation domain is intrinsically disordered:
246	  mean pLDDT **38.8**, with **98.1%** of residues below 50 ([`novel-modalities.md`](../modality-census/novel-modalities.md)
247	  §2.1; [`nr4a3-structure-assessment.json`](../../modalities/nr4a3-structure-assessment.json), EWSR1 region
248	  1–264). There is no folded cavity and no fpocket-druggable site on it — by contrast the NR4A3 LBD is
249	  confidently folded (mean pLDDT 85.0) yet still only borderline-druggable (best fpocket 0.495). So arm 2
250	  **cannot be a classical pocket ligand.** It must instead be a **condensate-partitioning / IDR-contacting
251	  moiety** — a chemotype that preferentially enriches in, or transiently contacts, the EWS-LC's
252	  phase-separated micro-environment [the prion-like-domain condensate behaviour of Boulay 2017]. This is an
253	  **emerging and genuinely hard** area: IDR/condensate-targeting medicinal chemistry is early-stage, the
254	  "site" is a dynamic ensemble rather than a structure, and predicting partitioning is not a solved
255	  problem. Arm 2 is the make-or-break unknown of this design, and we do not assert it is in hand.
256	
257	- **The bivalent geometry must actually be reachable.** Even granting both arms, the molecule must span
258	  from the LBD pocket to the EWS-LC region in the folded-plus-disordered fusion with a linker that achieves
259	  the EM the §3 window assumes. The LBD is ordered; the EWS-LC is a flexible IDR whose spatial relationship
260	  to the LBD is not fixed — which both *helps* (the IDR can reach the linker) and *hurts* (the EM is an
261	  effective average over a fluctuating geometry, not a rigid tether). Linker length/rigidity, attachment
262	  vectors, and the E3-handle placement are all unsolved ternary-complex design problems.
263	
264	- **EM is an assumption, and a fluctuating-geometry one.** The 1 mM–0.1 M EM range driving the §3 window
265	  is typical of *well-tethered* bivalent ligands; an arm anchored to a disordered, mobile IDR may realise a
266	  *lower* effective EM, shrinking the window toward the low end. The model's ceiling (~11×) should be read
267	  as optimistic.
268	
269	---
270	
271	## 5. In-silico program (clearly deferred — needs GPU later)
272	
273	No GPU/AWS work was done for this draft. The computational program that *would* de-risk arms 2 and the
274	geometry is specified here but **deferred**:
275	
276	1. **Ternary-complex / bivalent-pose modelling.** Build the fusion (opened-LBD ensemble from the companion
277	   metadynamics, reused directly) + EWS-LC ensemble, and sample arm-1/arm-2/linker poses to estimate the
278	   realisable effective molarity and whether a productive E3 ternary geometry is compatible with bivalent
279	   engagement. Reuses the existing opened pocket — no new pocket discovery needed for arm 1.
280	2. **Linker sampling.** Scan linker length/rigidity/attachment vectors against the EM the §3 model needs,
281	   to find the geometry that maximises the fusion-vs-WT window subject to synthesizability.
282	3. **Condensate-partitioning prediction for arm 2.** Apply emerging IDR/condensate-partitioning predictors
283	   to candidate arm-2 chemotypes — the highest-risk, least-mature step; success here is the precondition
284	   for the whole design.
285	
286	These are GPU-class jobs (MD on the folded+disordered fusion, ternary docking) and are explicitly *not*
287	run here; the single new computation in this paper is the CPU avidity model of §3.
288	
289	---
290	
291	## 6. The decisive experiment others run
292	
293	Computation cannot validate this; a wet-lab group would:
294	
295	0. **First, the fusion-addiction precondition (no new chemistry).** Run the **dTAG** fusion-addiction test
296	   [Nabet 2018] — a FKBP12^F36V degron knock-in at the fusion locus in patient-derived EMC lines (USZ-EMC;
297	   NCC-EMC1/2 [Bangerter 2023; Iwata]) + acute dTAG-13/V-1 degradation viability — to confirm that *acute*
298	   removal of the fusion kills EMC cells. If acute fusion loss is not lethal, the entire degrader premise
299	   (AND-gate included) is moot, so this gates everything downstream.
300	1. **Then, synthesise a candidate** AND-gate bivalent degrader (arm 1 = opened-LBD warhead, arm 2 =
301	   condensate/IDR anchor, linker + E3 handle).
302	2. **Test fusion-vs-wild-type degradation selectivity** in EMC cells (fusion+) versus control cells
303	   expressing wild-type NR4A3 only: measure loss of fusion protein vs loss of wild-type NR4A3, confirming
304	   the AND-gate spares the latter. This converts the §3 *binding* window into the *degradation* window the
305	   design actually needs.
306	
307	---
308	
309	## 7. Selectivity & safety
310	
311	The design's whole point is a safety improvement the LBD degrader cannot offer:
312	
313	- **Fusion-exclusive — spares wild-type NR4A3.** Because wild-type NR4A3 is engaged only monovalently by a
314	  deliberately weak arm 1, it is largely untouched; this avoids depleting NR4A3's **tumour-suppressor**
315	  function elsewhere (the AML liability of combined Nr4a1/Nr4a3 loss [Mullican 2007]; NR4A3's
316	  tumour-suppressive roles in HCC/breast/lymphoma [Safe & Karki 2021]). This is the central advantage over
317	  the shared-LBD degrader.
318	- **Addresses the paralogue axis too — asymmetrically, and as a specification only.** Arm 1 can
319	  additionally carry the companion paper's NR4A3-vs-paralogue selectivity handles
320	  ([`nr4a-selectivity.json`](../../modalities/nr4a-selectivity.json): 7 divergent Pocket-5
321	  residues, 5 pocket-facing in the opened ensemble), so the agent can be both **fusion-selective** (via the
322	  AND-gate) and paralogue-discriminating (via the handles) — two orthogonal selectivity layers. ⛔ **The
323	  paralogue layer is not one requirement**: sparing NR4A1 is the hard, mandatory half, and all 7 handles
324	  (5 engageable) differ from it; sparing NR4A2 is best-effort, and only 6 of 7 differ (4 of the 5
325	  engageable), because I531 is Ile in NR4A3 *and* NR4A2
326	  ([roadmap §2.4](../nr4a3-program-map.md#24--the-selectivity-requirement-is-asymmetric--and-this-page-stated-it-symmetrically)).
327	  Both halves are unvalidated predictions in the companion program — no positive control for selectivity
328	  detection has passed. ⚠ *Superseded, retained: "**Spares paralogues too** … the agent can be both
329	  fusion-selective and **paralogue-selective**", which asserted one achieved property over both.*
330	- **Net:** the AND-gate adds fusion-vs-wild-type-NR4A3 discrimination on top of the existing
331	  NR4A3-vs-paralogue discrimination, narrowing the on-target liability surface from "all NR4A3" to "fusion
332	  NR4A3 only."
333	
334	---
335	
336	## 8. Limitations
337	
338	1. **Binding ≠ degradation selectivity.** The §3 window is fusion-vs-WT *occupancy*; degradation
339	   selectivity additionally requires a productive, species-specific ternary complex. The honest claim is a
340	   binding window, not a degradation margin.
341	2. **Arm 2 is unproven and hard.** Targeting the EWS-LC IDR / its condensate (pLDDT 38.8, no pocket) with a
342	   small-molecule arm is an emerging, unsolved problem; there is no validated arm-2 chemotype. If arm 2
343	   fails, the AND-gate fails.
344	3. **The window is modest.** ~5.5× base case, ceiling ~11×. This is a feature of honest modelling, not a
345	   shortfall to be inflated — and the realised window on a mobile-IDR anchor may sit at the low end.
346	4. **The model inputs are illustrative.** Kd1, Kd2 and EM are assumptions chosen from literature ranges to
347	   probe the design principle; they are not measured affinities and predict no specific molecule.
348	5. **No molecule, no GPU run.** Nothing was synthesized; the ternary/linker/condensate computations (§5)
349	   are deferred GPU work; the only new result here is the CPU avidity model.
350	
351	---
352	
353	## 9. Broader indications
354	
355	The AND-gate logic is **target-general**: it works for *any* fusion that joins a **ligandable domain** (for
356	arm 1) to an **IDR / condensate-forming partner** (for arm 2) on one chain, where neither half is itself
357	fusion-unique but their *co-occurrence* is. The FET-fusion sarcomas are the natural set — Ewing sarcoma
358	(EWSR1::FLI1), desmoplastic small round cell tumour (EWSR1::WT1), clear-cell sarcoma (EWSR1::ATF1), myxoid
359	liposarcoma (FUS::DDIT3), and others — all fuse a FET prion-like IDR (the same class as the EWS-LC arm-2
360	target here) to a DNA-binding/effector partner that may furnish arm 1 [Boulay 2017 for the shared
361	prion-like-domain biology]. In each case the same coincidence-detection principle could, in principle, spare
362	the wild-type partners while removing the chimera — making EMC the worked example for a class-wide protein-
363	level fusion-exclusivity strategy. (These remain motivation, not demonstrated efficacy.)
